subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Approximately 85% of Canada's estimated 140,000 plant species are flowering plants.
• Flowering plants of the family Rosaceae, which includes roses, apples, cherries, and strawberries, are estimated to total 1,200 species in Canada.
• Flowering plants of the family Asteraceae, which includes sunflowers, daisies, dandelions, and asters, are estimated to total 2,400 species in Canada.
• Some of these flowering plants' habitats are being reduced by urban development and climate change.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the different families in which Canada's flowering plants are classified. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In Canada, 2,400 species are estimated to be sunflowers, daisies, dandelions, and asters, all classified as flowering plants of the family Asteraceae.
choices.B: Many roses, apples, cherries, and strawberries of the family Rosaceae are threatened by Canada's urban development and climate change.
choices.C: The family Rosaceae is estimated to make up 1,200 of Canada's 140,000 plant species.
choices.D: Among Canada's many flowering plants, roses, apples, cherries, and strawberries belong to the family Rosaceae, while sunflowers, daisies, dandelions, and asters belong to the family Asteraceae.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the different families that Canada's flowering plants belong to, specifying that roses, apples, cherries, and strawberries belong to the family Rosaceae, whereas sunflowers, daisies, dandelions, and asters belong to the family Asteraceae.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The sentence only mentions one family, Rosaceae; it doesn't emphasize the different families that Canada's flowering plants belong to.
